tool_summary: Opens an interactive SFTP session, or executes a batch of SFTP commands via -b, for file transfer over SSH. Same remote-visibility limitation as ssh applies to anything done inside the session.
platform_notes: sftp behavior is consistent across Linux and macOS (OpenSSH is standard on both).

rules.description: The -b flag executes a batch of SFTP commands from a file non-interactively. The batch file's contents (which could include arbitrary get/put/rm operations) are not visible in the command string and cannot currently be inspected by commandant.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on the batch file's contents, which commandant does not inspect. Treated as the worst case.

rules.description: Opens an interactive SFTP session. Everything done in that session afterward (uploads, downloads, deletes) is invisible to commandant, since it occurs entirely inside the session rather than as separate command invocations.
